$note: The source of truth for every requirement. profiles.mjs reads this and writes profiles/. Edit here, never there. Numbers carry their units and their provenance; anything unverified says so in `status` and the generator counts it.

status_key.solid: school-level physics or chemistry, not in doubt
status_key.measured: a real measurement from a real system, cited on its page
status_key.derived: computed here from solid inputs; the arithmetic is checkable
status_key.unvalidated: correct in kind, never demonstrated at this scale
status_key.unknown: we do not have this and are not pretending to
status_key.endowment_note: a class, not a status: something the place has that cannot be shipped, bought or manufactured

profiles.name: Hydrogen
profiles.one_line: The only scarce element on Venus, and the constraint everything else is measured against.
figures: cloud swept per kg of water
the fingerprint of an ocean that escaped
profiles.open_question: Is atmospheric extraction ever cheaper than shipping it? Nobody has costed sweeping cloud at industrial scale, and the answer decides whether the colony is self-sufficient or permanently supplied.

profiles.name: Gravity
profiles.one_line: The one thing Venus has that cannot be shipped, cornered or manufactured — and the reason it beats Mars and the Moon outright.
figures: it is the place, not a system in it
decades of bone and muscle loss
the whole category Mars and the Moon cannot solve
profiles.open_question: None physical, and one economic. Gas on Venus is a commodity — CO₂ and N₂ are unlimited, fungible and worth nothing per unit, and nobody can corner them. Gravity is the opposite: not transferable, not storable, not tradeable, and therefore not a commodity at all. It is a premium attached to a location, which means it cannot be de-fungibilised because it was never fungible, and cannot be speculated on because it cannot change hands. The only way to hold it is to be standing there.

profiles.name: Power
profiles.one_line: Solar, and there is a great deal of it — the one input that is not a problem.
figures: the platform sits near the top of the reflector
profiles.open_question: The four-day day means four-day nights. Storage sized for 48 hours of darkness is a different problem from Earth's twelve.

profiles.name: The envelope
profiles.one_line: A bag of breathable air floating in CO₂ — the habitat volume and the buoyancy are the same cubic metres, bought once.
figures: ≈ 9 m mean depth over the footprint
which is the entire safety case
profiles.open_question: Nobody has made a fluoropolymer membrane at square-kilometre scale, and the seam count is the number that decides the leak rate.

profiles.name: The site
profiles.one_line: 55 km, not 50 — chosen by the dissolved oxygen budget of the water rather than by the pressure.
figures: where it is 82 °C — you cannot have both
profiles.open_question: 0.53 bar is a workable habitat pressure but it is not sea level. Long-term physiology at half an atmosphere with normal partial-pressure oxygen is thinly studied.

profiles.name: The waterway
profiles.one_line: A closed loop that has to go anoxic in one specific place or it poisons itself with its own cleaning.
figures: condense, riffle, pool, bed, anoxic pocket, siphon
nitrate → N₂, and it must not share water with the above
profiles.open_question: Correct in kind, unvalidated in size. Nobody has run a closed water loop at 23,310 km² and every number that would follow from the stages at scale is deliberately not printed.

profiles.name: The floor
profiles.one_line: Soil, litter and burial — the half that decides whether there is a forest in fifty years, and the half that ate Biosphere 2's oxygen.
figures: so the carbon never came back round
equivalent to ~910 m of Earth ocean
the bed is the same structure
profiles.open_question: The floor is metabolically active and it eats. Sizing photosynthesis against soil respiration is the calculation Biosphere 2 got wrong, and getting it right requires knowing the soil's respiration rate before you install it.

profiles.name: The surface dome
profiles.one_line: Actively cooled, pressure-rated, acid-proof and heavy — the cheap layer biologically is the ruinous one structurally.
figures: above the melting point of lead
profiles.open_question: The longest anything has survived down there is a little over two hours. Everything about a permanent structure is extrapolation from that.

profiles.name: The lift
profiles.one_line: Fifty kilometres of hot column between the canopy and the floor, with freight going both ways.
profiles.open_question: This is the least-solved item on the list and the one nobody writing about cloud cities mentions. There is no proposed mechanism here worth printing.

profiles.name: The atmosphere
profiles.one_line: Breathable air, which on Venus is also the lifting gas — one purchase, two jobs.
figures: they move C and O; they do not make H
no pressure differential across the skin
profiles.open_question: Oxygen partial pressure at 0.53 bar total means a richer mix, and a richer mix in a fluoropolymer envelope is a fire question nobody has answered at this scale.

profiles.name: Station keeping
profiles.one_line: Formation flying, not anchoring — nothing at 55 km holds a position over the ground.
figures: the band laps the planet in ~4 days
passes a point below in 25 minutes
profiles.open_question: Thousands of linked aerostats holding formation in a shear layer, for decades. The failure mode is not one module falling; it is the whole raft slowly tearing.

profiles.name: The clocks
profiles.one_line: Two of them, differing by twenty-nine — and the reason is altitude rather than politics.
figures: sunrise to sunrise on the ground
the synodic period, which nobody owns
profiles.open_question: None outstanding. This one is settled, and it is the only requirement on the list that is.

profiles.name: The relay
profiles.one_line: Venus is not a haul, it is a node — information commutes and atoms visit.
profiles.open_question: None physical. The design question is what you agree to decide locally, given that any question you send home is answered nine minutes and a decision-cycle later.

profiles.name: The ecosystem
profiles.one_line: Twelve orders, twenty-one capabilities, and every capability a conjunction of the ones it needs.
figures: no number of bees is a beetle
profiles.open_question: Everything. The ecosystem page is a dependency graph, not a demonstration, and no closed ecology has ever run for more than two years at three acres.
